subtype: Approach: groupthink on a weak idea [Pitfall]
passage: In the school workshop in Da Nang, Tuan laid a sketch on the table: a bridge of wooden sticks with one tall arch and no side supports. "This will hold the most weight," he said, and everyone nodded. Nadia frowned at the arch, which looked thin at the base, but said nothing. Linh glanced at Nadia and bit her lip. On test day the arch bowed and cracked under the second weight. The team stared at the pile of sticks. "I thought it might," Nadia said at last. "So did I," said Linh. Tuan looked from one to the other. "Then why did nobody say so?" No one answered. Each of them had thought someone else would speak first.

qa.q: Where was the bridge test held and what happened to the arch?
qa.a: The arch bowed and cracked under the second weight on test day.

qa.q: Why did Nadia stay silent when the plan was shown?
qa.a: Nadia felt doubtful but hesitant to object, probably not wanting to be the only one to disagree with a confident plan.

qa.q: What could the team do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: They could ask each member for a concern before choosing a design, because that lets doubts be voiced without anyone standing alone.

qa.q: How might Tuan feel when learning that two people had doubts?
qa.a: Tuan probably feels surprised and a little hurt, since a concern could have saved the bridge.

grounding: Everyone agrees with the confident member's plan even though two have doubts, the design fails at testing, and the team later admits nobody wanted to be the one to object.

subtype: Approach: groupthink on a weak idea [Pitfall]
passage:
In the robotics club room, Francis tapped the whiteboard with his marker. "Four legs, not wheels. It'll climb the ramp easily. Trust me."

Alka had doubts. Legs were hard to balance. She glanced at Jomon, who looked unsure too. But Francis sounded so certain, and everyone else was already nodding.

"Sounds great," Alka said.

For three weeks they built legs. Nobody raised the balance problem again.

On test day, the robot took two steps up the ramp, tipped sideways and fell off the table. One leg snapped.

Later, eating biscuits in silence, Jomon finally said, "I thought legs were a bad idea from the start."

"Me too," Alka admitted.

Francis stared. "Why didn't you say anything?"

"You seemed so sure," Alka said. "Nobody wanted to go first."

The coach, packing up, said only, "Next time, someone has to be."

qa.q: How many steps did the robot take before tipping?
qa.a: The robot took two steps up the ramp before it tipped sideways.

qa.q: Why did Alka say "Sounds great" despite her doubts?
qa.a: Alka felt hesitant and unwilling to stand out, since Francis sounded certain and everyone else was nodding.

qa.q: What could the team change before their next design?
qa.a: They could ask each member to name one risk before deciding, so doubts like the balance problem are said out loud early.

qa.q: How might Francis feel learning that two members doubted the plan all along?
qa.a: Francis is probably shocked and a bit hurt, wishing someone had spoken, since he had no idea others disagreed.

grounding: Shows a team agreeing with a confident member's plan despite private doubts, the design failing at testing, and members admitting nobody wanted to object.

subtype: Approach: groupthink on a weak idea [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Joseph,

You asked how the bridge competition went. Badly. And I want to tell you why, because I think it was partly my fault.

Rohit was so confident. He said a single arch of ice-cream sticks would hold five kilos, no need for side trusses. I thought the arch alone looked weak. So did Nilesh, I found out later. But Rohit had won last year, and when he asked, "Everyone okay?", we all said yes.

At testing, the bridge cracked at two kilos. The judges were kind about it, which was worse.

On the bus back, Nilesh said, "I knew it would bend." I said, "Me too." Rohit went very quiet.

We agreed with him because arguing felt awkward. That awkwardness cost us the whole competition. Next time I'll say it, even if my voice shakes.

Imran

qa.q: At what weight did the bridge crack?
qa.a: The bridge cracked at two kilos.

qa.q: How does Imran feel looking back on the competition?
qa.a: Imran feels regretful and partly to blame, knowing the doubt was never spoken because arguing felt awkward.

qa.q: What would you advise Imran's team to try before building next time?
qa.a: Ask each member to name one weakness in the design before voting, so no one has to be the lone objector.

qa.q: How might Rohit have felt on the bus when he heard the others had doubts?
qa.a: Rohit probably felt hurt and embarrassed, realising his teammates had doubts but nobody told him in time.

grounding: A letter shows a team following a confident member's plan despite hidden doubts, the design failing at testing and members admitting nobody objected.
